My Score: 9/10

I've honestly never had so much fun raging at getting one-shot in my life.

That about sums it up, but I'll go a bit more into detail here:

You are a survivor of a crashed space transport ship on a strange alien world, and you're trying to get back out of there.  That's about all there is for story.  Where this game shines is its difficulty:  When you die, you're done; you start over.  Killing things and opening containers grants you money and experience - with the money you open the chests that are randomly scattered around the levels to help you kill more things and get you more money and experience.  It's a fairly short game (a solid playthrough can take less than an hour, but it can take longer)... but here's the catch.  The longer you take on your playthrough, the harder the game gets.  More enemies start spawning, they do more damage, and they have more health... and eventually "boss" enemies start spawning as regular enemies.

I say it's a short game, but it's by no means one without content.  There's tons of items to collect and tons of different enemies and enemy combinations, and it's all random.  Everything.  The level you start on, the levels that are next, the item chest locations, the contents in those chests, the final teleporter to end the level's location, the enemies you encounter, which bosses you see, etc.  Nothing's the same twice, except for the final level and the final boss.

There's loads of secrets, too, from unlockable characters to fun little easter eggs and other stuff that even I haven't found yet.  Overall, definitely worth a buy - don't get put off by the graphics; if it were any more your computer would die, trust me.  It works.

Risk Of Rain is called the sidescrolling version of The Binding Of Isaac and it kinda is. But Risk Of Rain gives you multiple characters (all except one need to be unlocked first, however) and many skills to use, and more variety in its levels. And it can become quite challenging real fast. Enemies randomly spawn in the levels and you can use your skillset to take them down, earning you experience and gold. Unlock chests and buy items on your way to keep yourself from dying, because you *will* die. It's just a matter of time really. The items you find are randomly generated and are always useful. They have no negative effects (if they do it just depends on the total number of enemies walking around and the sort of level you are in). So the goal is to find as many as you can. Each level ends with a boss fight (or fights) which you, obviously, have to defeat. Once defeated you have to take out the remaining enemies before you can teleport to the next area. But, once you teleport you 'bank' your money, so you start from scratch again (your items will remain with you, of course). In the beginning you will probably last just several minutes, but once you unlock better items and characters these sessions will increase up to 45-60 minutes I guess. 
I haven't mentioned it yet, but you probably were already aware of it, and that's the fact that if you die, you have to start completely over. I love it !

So, if you're into roguelikes give Risk Of Rain a try. It's definitely worth the risk.

[Rating: 82/100]

A great pick up and play rogue like game. My only quip about this game is that the levels are not randomly generated in the sense each time you play you have a different and new level. There are only a few variants to each map type. Still a fun game that you can just pick up and play and the game tends to only take an hour to beat.

There are some games, that when they come out, you wait for a sale.

This is not one of those games. Worth every single cent of the asking price.
I guess this would be a roguelike-like, technically. I just call it fun.
If Binding of Isaac and Contra had a baby, its name would be Risk of Rain
